This normalization is critical in any algorithm that relies on edge existence checks, such as triangle counting or union-find with edge-based processing."}

raw: {"name":"strongly_connected_component_check","when_to_use":"when the problem statement shifts from reachability to checking whether two nodes are in the same strongly connected component in a directed graph","instructions":"Use Kosaraju's algorithm to compute strongly connected components. First, perform a DFS to obtain finishing times, then reverse the graph and perform DFS in order of decreasing finishing times. Group nodes by component. For a query (s, t), check if s and t belong to the same component. Output \"YES\" if they do, otherwise \"NO\". Handle the case where s == t trivially by returning \"YES\". Ensure no hardcoding, use only standard library, and maintain consistent input/output format."}

skills.instructions: Use Kosaraju's algorithm to compute strongly connected components. First, perform a DFS to obtain finishing times, then reverse the graph and perform DFS in order of decreasing finishing times. Group nodes by component. For a query (s, t), check if s and t belong to the same component. Output "YES" if they do, otherwise "NO". Handle the case where s == t trivially by returning "YES". Ensure no hardcoding, use only standard library, and maintain consistent input/output format.
